vulnerabilities.title: Flask Session Cache Poisoning
vulnerabilities.description: Response containing data intended for one client may be cached and sent to other clients. Session cookies may be shared between users.
vulnerabilities.impact: Session hijacking, unauthorized access, data leakage
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update Flask to version 2.2.5 or higher (recommend 3.1.3)

vulnerabilities.title: Flask Information Disclosure via Cache Headers
vulnerabilities.description: Missing cache-variation headers when session object is accessed via certain code paths, leading to potential cache poisoning.
vulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure, cache poisoning, privacy violations

vulnerabilities.title: Outdated Python Base Image
vulnerabilities.description: Python 3.8 reached end-of-life in October 2024. No security patches available.
vulnerabilities.impact: Missing security updates, exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities

vulnerabilities.title: Outdated GitHub Actions
vulnerabilities.description: Multiple GitHub Actions are using outdated versions with potential security issues.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update all GitHub Actions to their latest versions

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Security Headers
vulnerabilities.description: Application does not set security headers like CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, etc.
vulnerabilities.impact: Increased vulnerability to XSS, clickjacking, and MITM attacks
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement Flask-Talisman or manually add security headers

security_strengths.details: No security issues found in Python code
No hardcoded credentials or API keys detected
Properly using GitHub Actions secrets for sensitive data

short_term.details: pip install flask-talisman and configure in app.py
Integrate safety or pip-audit into GitHub Actions workflow
Set SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, HTTPONLY, and SAMESITE flags

long_term.details: Use Trivy, Snyk, or similar in CI/CD pipeline
